html:
The Angevin Empire is the modern name for the lands held by the Plantagenet kings of England in the 1100s and early 1200s: England, about half of France, and parts of Ireland and Wales. It is on the map for 1200.

It was built by Henry II, count of Anjou. From his parents he got Anjou, Normandy and a claim to England, which he took in 1154. His marriage to Eleanor of Aquitaine brought her huge duchy in the south of France. He held more of France than the French king, though he owed that king homage for it.

Henry's son Richard the Lionheart spent most of his reign on crusade and at war. His brother John lost Normandy and Anjou to Philip II of France in 1204, and the defeat of John's allies at Bouvines in 1214 ended hopes of getting them back. The crisis led to Magna Carta in 1215. The English kings kept Gascony, and the quarrel later fed the Hundred Years' War.
